- When sentiment is high (≥ 0.6) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If sentiment is low (≤ 0.4) and forecast is trending up, cap the forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to prevent overbought bias.  
- If forecast consistently overshoots true values by >3% in the first 5–7 days, apply a 2–3% downward correction to the next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is volatile (fluctuating >0.3 in 3 consecutive days), reduce forecast smoothness — use 3-day moving average instead of 7-day to avoid lagged reactions.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3 consecutive days >+5% from 14-day mean), adjust forecast to align with 14-day moving average, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.  
- For horizon >14 days, if sentiment is positive but forecast is flat or declining, add a 1–2% upward bias to reflect sentiment-driven momentum.  
- If forecast is consistently below true outcome by >2% over 3+ consecutive days, check sentiment for hidden bullish signals — if sentiment is rising, increase forecast by 1–3% to capture sentiment-driven breakout.
